setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Scarlet Begonias has a stronger-than-normal jam and stands well on its own; Scarlet Begonias closes the first set unaccompanied, which the reviewer believes happened only this once [12][15][16]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): The opening Minglewood is very hot [15]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Peggy-O is badly flubbed [17]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Brown Eyed Women is called one of the best ever played, with a chill-inducing Jerry solo [9]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Jerry's emotional playing in the Row Jimmy jam leads beautifully into the 'broken heart' verse; reviewer's favorite Row Jimmy [11]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): St. Stephen is slow and sweet, played differently from what one would expect [15]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The St. Stephen>Other One is triumphant, a combination that can be off but was on this night [16]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): St. Stephen>Other One>Stella has unique jams and a good transition from spacy Other One into Stella [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-03-20.145511.mtx.motb0226.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 181 min [1]
- **gd1977-03-20.141710.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 188 min [2]
- **gd77-03-20.sbd.kempa.257.sbefixed.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 145 min; rated 4.65/5 by 17 [4]. Said about its sound: This newer transfer lacks the reel-generation hiss of the earlier version; Reviewer's own copy has a little hiss that doesn't interfere with listening [8][11]
- **gd77-03-20.sbd.miller.25610.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 153 min; rated 4.54/5 by 24 [5]. Said about its sound: The sound is described as crisp; The sound quality is described as peerless [12][16]

## Around the show

- Terrapin Station was broadcast on the King Biscuit Flower Hour [2]
- The Brown Eyed Women is compared with the one from 05-08-77 [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-03-20.145511.mtx.motb0226.flac16**: taped by Audience source by Bob Menke; transferred by Mastering & Matrix: Derek McCabe; source: Matrix by Derek McCabe [1]
- **gd1977-03-20.141710.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Master Reel (7in 7.5ips 1/2trk dbx) > Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: Soundboard source DATs were supplied by David Gans [2]
- **gd77-03-20.sbd.kempa.257.sbefixed.shnf**: source: SBD > Reel(1) > ?? > DAT > WAV > SHN [4]
- **gd77-03-20.sbd.miller.25610.sbeok.shnf**: source: Recording Info: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat x 2 -> Sonic Solutions -> CD Transfer Info: CD -> EAC -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHNTracked and SHN'd By… [5]. Also: This source is judged better than the other one, and includes the Terrapin second encore [17]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-03-20 Winterland Arena, San Francisco, CA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/06/grateful-dead-1977-03-20-winterland.html) [21]
- Fan art by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-12-31 Winterland Arena, San Francisco, CA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/06/grateful-dead-1977-12-31-winterland.html) [22]
